content:
ian: heads-up — we're seeing a cluster of OOMs in dedicated-pool-us-west-2 starting ~2543210000. spike correlates with the kernel-autotune rollout from last night.
elena: confirmed. alerting showed 5xx OOMs on inference-route /v1/generate, mostly long-context requests.
maria: logs show workspace_size jumped from ~1.2GB -> ~2.8GB for a subset of kernels. suspect kernel selector picked a 'wide' matmul path for >2k token batches.
aj: any recent changes to kv prefetch or cache warmup? those can amplify transient memory.
ian: yes — we enabled aggressive kv prefetch for large-chat sessions (kv.prefetch=true, batch_hint=large) in canary; combined with new kernel it looks like memory composes: workspace + kv pages + pending batch buffers.
elena: immediate ask: can we throttle prefetch to reduce steady memory? even temporary TTL reduction would free some pages.
maria: quick mitigation I can push: set kv.prefetch=false for dedicated-pool-us-west-2 and lower kv.max_prefetch_pages=32. also reduce kv.ttl from 300s -> 60s.
ian: please do. also flip runtime flag kernel.selector.prefer_low_memory=true to bias against the new autotuned path.
aj: adding circuit-breaker on long requests: config snippet I propose:
```
route:/v1/generate
circuit_breaker:
  max_concurrent_long_reqs: 6
  long_req_threshold_ms: 12000
  fail_mode: degrade_to_small_model
```
ian: 👍 set failover to small-quantized variant (gpt-small-q8) rather than returning 5xx. degrade behavior preserves latency.
ops-bot: rollback scheduled? any deploys in flight?
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: rollback kernel-autotune canary -> canary-0 reverted at 2543210024 by maria.
maria: rolled kv.prefetch=false and set kernel.selector flag at 2543210026. monitoring now.
elena: telemetry show memory tail dropping within one GC window, OOM rate down from 12/min -> 1/min. good signal but not zero.
ian: still seeing a couple of residual OOMs tied to multi-request batching bursts. propose short-term request shaping: cap effective batch_size for routes with context_length > 1500 to 2.
aj: can do via rate-limiter policy and request-weight adjustments. I'll push patch to route config:
```
- route: /v1/generate
  when: context_length > 1500
  policies:
    - max_batch: 2
    - allow_burst: false
```
ian: also enable buffer_reuse=true on that pool so transient allocations reuse GPU buffers instead of reallocating. this helped previously during pkgs 1746 incidents.
maria: buffer_reuse toggle pushed at 2543210030.
elena: runbook note: for future kernel autotune rollouts, add a dry-run mode to measure max_workspace per kernel on sampled traffic before flipping selector globally.
ian: agreed — added to deploy checklist. filed a follow-up: jira INFR-1428 "kernel-autotune dry-run + mem-safety checks".
aj: postmortem action: add a histogram metric kernel_workspace_bytes_by_kernel and a prom alert if p95 > 70% of GPU memory for any kernel.
maria: recording steps:
- immediate: rollback canary, kv.prefetch=false, ttl->60s, kernel.selector.prefer_low_memory=true, buffer_reuse=true, short-batch policy for long contexts.
- short-term: circuit-breaker + degrade-to-small-model, limit concurrent long requests.
- long-term: dry-run autotune + telemetry + workspace histograms (INFR-1428).
ian: nice. can we ship a small hotfix patch to make kernel.selector soft-prefer low-memory by percent (e.g., prefer_low_memory=0.8) so selection is probabilistic? avoids full rollback for future.
maria: I'll prototype.
elena: closing incident once 24h stable with <0.1 OOM/min across pool. tagging this thread for the playbook: "prefetch-throttle + kernel-selector fallback".
aj: also notify customers on dedicated who might be impacted; SRE will send a short note.
ian: thanks everyone. follow-ups: INFR-1428 and a postmortem doc. will paste logs into the postmortem.
deploy-bot: live metrics: memory usage back to baseline, canary reverted.
ian: 👍 monitoring set to intensified for next 6 hours.
_comment: Generated Slack thread JSON for eng-runtime OOM mitigation playbook; flat JSON fields only.
